answer: Require each new identity to pass a rotating set of interactive human-proof challenges: one round asks the applicant to spot the hollow marble among solid ones, the next to find a walnut hidden in a cluttered scene, and the puzzle type changes every epoch so no single solver works twice. A Sybil attacker must pay a human or a solving farm for every identity, while per-IP rate limits and a cooling period make bulk creation slow and expensive. The limit is that solving farms and AI solvers keep improving, so puzzles must keep rotating and never be trusted alone.
